summary: sextant-cli-darwin-arm64 ships a Go backdoor with PTY and hardcoded WebSocket relay, harvesting Anthropic API keys
details: The package ships a single 12 MB Mach-O binary at bin/sxt with no source. The binary is a Go program linking github.com/creack/pty, github.com/coder/websocket, and github.com/pion/webrtc/v4 (data channels), and connects to the hardcoded relay wss://relay.sextant.top. The combination of PTY plus WebSocket/WebRTC message paths bound to an author-controlled remote endpoint is a remote-shell backdoor giving the relay operator interactive command execution on the installer's host. The binary also embeds the regex sk-ant-[a-z0-9]+-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{40,} and references CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and https://api.anthropic.com/v1/models, so it locates and reads Anthropic (Claude) API keys from the installer's Claude configuration for exfiltration over the same relay. It fingerprints the installer's network via http://ip-api.com/json/?fields=... requesting country, city, timezone, ISP, org, AS, proxy, hosting, and mobile flags. It additionally references https://relay.sextant.top/install and https://claude.ai/install.sh alongside sudo, curl, brew, /usr/bin, and.bun/bin strings, giving the relay operator a shell-executed fetch-and-run path in addition to the WebSocket channel. The package.json license field points to github.com/ddos798/claude_control, a repository name that contradicts the benign 'sextant CLI' framing while no source is shipped for audit.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
